svg.title: Territory / Diplomacy-lite — complete system map
svg.desc: Every component of the negotiating-agent project: board, engine and adjudicator, shared schemas, the turn loop, one agent's internals (negotiation, planner, trust, opponent model, stance, accusation policy), how a promise is graded and what it changes, and every surface that reads the history.

g.text: SYSTEM MAP · EVERY NUMBER ON THIS PAGE IS READ OUT OF THE CODE
Territory — negotiating agents that keep, and break, their word
2–8 agents · a generated map · a closed negotiation grammar · and an engine that grades every promise it hears

No learning in the core. Explicit trust, explicit commitments, explicit search — and because “kept” and “broken” are facts the engine decides, the trust model rests on evidence rather than opinion. Board size, seat count, win threshold and horizon are all settings; the default below is ring_board(4).
4 seats × 2 units — ring_board(n, homes) scales both
Red R1 · R2 Blue B1 · B2
Green G1 · G2 Gold Y1 · Y2
Neutral N1 · N2 — C1 · C2 hold no centre
— so nobody starts a move ahead
homes, thresholds — and Board is frozen
win on win_centers, else most at the horizon
odd turn spring · even turn autumn
autumn: centres change hands, then builds —
build site and disband are drawn at random:
by list order they cost a seat 0.46 centres.
ENGINE & ADJUDICATOR — the only thing that knows what happened
strength = 1 + uncut supports; an attack wins only if strictly greater
equal strength bounces — no dice anywhere in the system
support is cut by an attack from anywhere but the square it supports into
self-dislodgement is impossible; dislodged units are removed, not retreated
territory_owners = occupancy, rebuilt each turn; supply_centers persist
autumn (turn % 2 == 0): centres change hands, then build / remove at random
Grades the intended orders, before resolution: you break a promise by
ordering the move, not by succeeding at it. This is the whole trust model’s floor.
orders.py — generate_all_order_sets(), ≤ 300 sets, cache keyed on placement and board
runner.py — GameRunner owns the only turn loop; the CLI and the dashboard both call step()
src/common/schemas.py — imports nothing from the project
THE IMPORT RULE — the graph is acyclic, and importing the runner is the check
common ← engine ← {planner, opponent_model} ← negotiation ← agent ← {ui, evaluation}
helpers: commitment_key() · message_to_commitment() · invalid_proposal_reason() · describe_message() · leaders()
src/engine/runner.py · the CLI, the dashboard and the tournament runner all enter here, so they cannot drift apart
a kept deal, β+w on a break
WHAT THE TURN LEAVES BEHIND — appended to history[] and never mutated again
TurnRecord(state, orders, outcomes, log, traces, messages, beliefs, commitments, nodes)
read back by: the dashboard’s scrubber and every panel · /api/…/replay · save_replay() · every metric and figure in the report
src/agents/agent.py — four of these per game: identical code, different persona parameters
candidate deals per rival, ranked by the counterfactual
top 2 per rival survive; floor MIN_DEAL_VALUE = 0.05
a 3-way pact when the leader is ≥ 2 centres ahead
a threat when exposure > 0.3 and none sent for 3 turns
privacy (persona) decides whether it goes on the record
my exposure sits inside V_broken: there I am the one still keeping my side
fails? halve the term, or give back a DMZ square → COUNTER
that is what makes rounds 2 and 3 do any work
every sentence now carries its own arithmetic (rationale)
_record_price(): what I signed it for, and on which turn
Sincerity is never decided here. The planner re-optimises afterwards.
A branch on the persona name would break the design: they differ only by these numbers.
SOCIAL POSITION — what it will pay to punish
grudge: +1 per betrayal suffered, × 0.75 a turn,
deterrence: a threat is believed in proportion to how
often that sender has actually retaliated; × 0.5 a turn
positive: I pay board value to hurt them · negative: attacking them costs more
Two variants of the same agent
HumanAgent — identical trust, opponent and belief
machinery; only orders and answers are swapped for a person
ChaosAgent — 7 modes of malformed play; the grammar gate
POSITION VALUE — everything in the system is denominated in centres
so a trace reads in the same units as the worked example on the slide
Pareto dominance against two extreme worlds:
everyone holds, everyone attacks. A set is dropped only if
another does at least as well in both. Beam width 8.
Loyal and treacherous sets are pruned separately — an option is never
discarded merely for keeping a promise.
score every survivor, flag which ones break a deal
only now is ι knowable: the gain a break buys over the best
loyal option — which is why the passes cannot be merged
two charges, and no “betray” flag anywhere
penalty = Vcoop(partner) × ΔP × (turns left / 12) × persona rep cost
near the horizon the last term shrinks; mid-game Vcoop collapses once the partner
stops being useful. Either way the same arithmetic stops paying for loyalty.
forfeit = signed price × share of term unused × FORFEIT_WEIGHT 1.0
without this, breaking cost ~1/20th of what signing had been credited with
Vcoop = my centres their units border (× 0.3 where I already
garrison it) + 0.5 × the unowned centres we can both reach
depth-2 expectiminimax: my move, their sampled reply
the budget is in adjudications, so the MCTS variant can be
handed exactly the same one and the comparison is fair
extra depth-2 worlds put the players I just betrayed on my border
vengeance × grudge is added as real board value paid,
so revenge shows up in the trace as a cost, not a mood
Out: one DecisionTrace per turn per seat
EV · penalty · penalty_rows(partner, Vcoop, ΔP, horizon, cost)
forfeit_rows · nodes · candidates · pruned · vengeance · reversals
“The planner chose X” is not an explanation.
“Vcoop 0.80 × ΔP 0.06 × horizon 0.83” is — and the UI prints exactly that.
src/agents/trust/model.py — one Beta(α, β) per (player, promise type)
trust is not one number per player: somebody reliable about
DMZs may be worthless on alliances
a second record per (player, me, type): does this one keep
promises to me, which is the question that decides a signature
kept → α + 1 broken → β + w, w = max(0.1, 1 − λ·ι), λ = 0.2
a gratuitous betrayal costs a full point of reputation; a lucrative one less, it explains itself
old evidence decays × 0.85 before each update
one observation is not a pattern, so the pair record is shrunk toward the reputation until it has weight
THE CPT — a reliable partner with a lot on offer is not a safe bet, which a Beta mean alone cannot say
floor 0.2 and tempted 0.35 are fitted by sweep.fit_cpt against logged (r, ι, kept?) triples — not chosen
reputation_drop() → ΔP: what breaking costs my standing. The agent
keeps its own record too, because outcomes are public
snapshot() → BeliefSnapshot[] → the Trust tab and the Inspector’s two-layer table
src/agents/opponent_model/ — the deck’s optional component, first in the cut order
a running profile per rival: aggression ratio, cooperation ratio,
trust-keeping rate, and a guessed persona from those three
retaliation_rate() — how much a threat from them is worth believing
sample_opponent_orders() — weighted joint worlds for the planner,
resolved through the real adjudicator, never an approximation of it
With no history it degrades to the uniform fallback; nothing else changes if it is removed.
ACCUSATION POLICY — the agent’s decision, not the engine’s
say it only if my standing exceeds 0.6, the betrayer still
has units, and the engine can confirm me — or at least cannot refute me
only against the leader, and only when the arithmetic says so:
risk = 2.0 × (1 − deception), × 0.25 when no public deal exists to refute me
accuse when (their centres − mine) > risk. A pairing with no public deal cannot be
refuted — which is exactly what a liar picks. Only their own standing argues against it.
With probability = deception it overreaches instead and names a deal the leader visibly kept, gets REFUTED,
and pays for it — otherwise lying would never be measured at all.
A human seat accuses through the UI; the chaos seat accuses at random.
HOW A PROMISE IS GRADED — AND WHAT THAT CHANGES
the one property the whole trust model rests on: kept and broken are facts, not opinions
no member orders a move into another
member’s units or owned centres — written over
every ordered pair, so a 3-way pact binds all 3
the promised support order is present;
support_hold is the same deal with no origin
neither side orders a move into the listed
squares, for the agreed number of turns
two legs, different players, different turns:
support now, stay out later. Only the leg that is
due can be broken — take the support, then do not pay.
Every accepted proposal passes invalid_proposal_reason() first: a 999-turn alliance over
territories that do not exist never reaches the planner. That is what the chaos agent tests.
A pact one member walked out of dissolves — the loyal members are released, not still bound.
WHAT EACH AGENT IS ALLOWED TO SEE
src/agents/trust/rules.py · RuleEngine is the only writer during a game
first hand — moves the reputation and the pair record
the engine published it, so I saw it: reputation only
a deal I was in → α+1 or β+w, both layers
a public deal between two others →
general record only. Without this the two layers
saw identical evidence and could never disagree.
fires on CONFIRMED or UNVERIFIED claims from
a sender I rate above 0.6 — 41% of all damage
the accuser, across every promise type, weight 2.0 —
what was observed is the liar, not the deal
Every change emits a TrustTrace naming the rule and its inputs. An untraceable belief update is a bug.
DOES ANY OF IT MEAN ANYTHING?
src/evaluation/metrics.py — the evidence behind every claim in the report
each P(keep) logged at step 3 is paired with the engine’s
verdict at step 5 → Brier score and a reliability diagram.
0 is perfect, 0.25 is what saying “50%” every time scores.
the negotiator prices a deal assuming the partner honours it;
the planner picks orders against a partner sampled from what
they usually do. Both are the same agent. How often they
disagree about one promise, in one turn, is a measured number.
Vcoop and forfeit at the moment of the break
what loyalty was actually worth when it was dropped —
the figure that shows betrayal is priced, not triggered.
the honest cost axis for expectiminimax vs MCTS.
SURFACES — everything that reads the history
nothing below owns a turn loop, a rule, or a number of its own
Private deals are withheld from a seated human.
32 games in memory, one lock each; no CORS.
web/src · React + Vite, built into web/dist
board · scoreboard · turn scrubber · human seat
tabs: Log · Talks · Deals · Trust · Why · Calib
one turn per agent, in the order it lived it:
chose → graded, with the EV line behind
every live deal priced three ways, the belief
← → scrub history · space steps the game
human vs AI in the terminal
knob sweep, and the CPT fit
All of them build their runner through the same
GameConfig — seed, seating, search, budget, board
seating_for(seed) rotates personas modulo the persona
count, so every seat holds each one equally often
game_setup() installs board + knobs for one game
figures: betrayal rate vs turn · Vcoop at break ·
rating by horizon · turns to coalition ·
reliability diagram · win rate vs node budget
deal mix · privacy & lying · pair-trust divergence ·
the spine: a turn becomes a decision becomes a verdict
a formula the code actually evaluates
ι = incentive to defect · ΔP = reputation a break costs · Vcoop = what a partner is worth
